newsitem.title: USA: ITT creative plan unlikely to stop Hilton.
newsitem.headline: ITT creative plan unlikely to stop Hilton.

text.p: ITT Corp's new, creative restructuring plan aimed at destroying a hostile $6.5 billion bid from Hilton Hotels Corp is unlikely to stop its aggressive rival.

Just hours after ITT announced its plan to split the company into three business and buy back stock, Hilton said it would fight the plan in court. If unsuccessful, Wall Street experts speculated Hilton may launch a bid for the new hotel and casino company to be named ITT Destinations Inc.
"Hilton is not going to just lie down," said James Murren of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

The seven-month takeover battle took on a new direction early Wednesday when ITT announced the massive overhaul. Although the company has sold some assets and was widely expected to either buy back stock or issue a special dividend, few had anticipated a company break-up and self-tender.
"I think the shareholders are loving this. It's very creative on the laundry list of anti-takeover moves," said Arthur Adler, a partner in the lodging and gaming advisory group at Coopers & Lybrand.
Indeed, news of ITT's plan, combined with the prospect of a continued battle, drove shares of ITT up 4-3/8 to 67.
Once considered a plodding and lethargic company, Wall Street experts praised the aggressive plan approved by ITT's board after an 11-hour meeting.
They cited ITT's move to split into three pieces - a move that ITT estimates will save $500 million in taxes that would have accompanied a sale of the directories and education units.
They also cited ITT's proposal to create a staggered board for the Destinations hotel and casino business as a step which would hinder any potential bid launched by Hilton.

"I think this is a step in the right direction. We're going to hang in there" and not tender shares, said Robert Lyon, president of Institutional Capital Corp, which owns more than two million shares of ITT.
By late afternoon, analysts were still calculating the value of the three separate companies to be created from ITT.

In addition to ITT Destinations, the plan calls for the highly profitable telephone directories business to be contained in ITT Corp and the formation of ITT Educational Services Inc, which will house the post-secondary technical education unit.

Murren valued the hotel and casino business at $70 to $75 per share, and speculated that Hilton would be forced to bid above $80 in order to wrest control from ITT. Other estimates were somewhat more conservative.
Despite the widespread praise for the restructuring, several analysts and investors still think ITT should have more closely considered Hilton's takeover bid.
"It's clearly a sensible plan. What's not so clear is why they will not give Hilton a chance to present its case to shareholders," said David Loeb of Credit Lyonnais Securities USA Inc.
"I still feel they should have talked to Hilton. Barring that, they have done a really good job," said investor Lyon.
